title: Output verification and model calibration
what: Measure how often the decision is right before you trust it with anything.

shape.state: one record from a labelled set, with the answer withheld
shape.question: the same question you will ask in production
shape.answer: the model's pick, for you to compare against the human answer

use: Build a validation set of a few dozen to a few hundred records a human has already labelled, run the loop without showing the answers, and count the matches. Misclassifications tell you where the labels are ambiguous, and the spread of probabilities tells you where the confidence cutoff belongs. The video's own advice is fifty records or more before production; tune the cutoff on one set and hold some records back.

code.label: a labelled set, a match rate, a cutoff
code.src:
rows = json.load(open("labelled.json"))      # state + human label

hits, conf = 0, []
for r in rows:
    ans = decide(r["state"], LABEL_QUESTION)["category"]
    hits += ans["choice"] == r["label"]
    conf.append((ans["confidence"], ans["choice"] == r["label"]))

print("agreement %.1f%% of %d" % (100 * hits / len(rows), len(rows)))
for cut in (0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8, 0.9):
    kept = [c for c in conf if c[0] >= cut]
    right = [c[1] for c in kept]
    print("cutoff %.1f keeps %d rows at %.1f%% correct"
          % (cut, len(kept), 100 * sum(right) / max(len(right), 1)))

title: Agent skill selection
what: Let the agent pick the right skill before it loads any of them.

shape.question: choice, one option per skill in the library
shape.answer: the skill to load, plus how sure it is

use: You do not have to put every skill description in the context window to choose one. Register the skills as the options, send the prompt, and load only the winner. In the video's own counting, 145 skills were matched in about five seconds across fourteen tests against roughly thirty for the larger model, and a separate test over 182 skills cut wrong picks by more than half. Keep the option list to the skills that are real candidates for this agent.

code.label: the skill library is the menu
code.src:

  --ask 'skill=choice:Which skill should the agent load?|xlsx:Spreadsheet work,youtube-content:Transcripts to summaries,email-inbox-triage:Inbox triage,docx:Word documents,arxiv:Paper search' \

title: Intelligent multi model routing
what: Send the easy question to the cheap model and the hard one to the expensive model.

shape.question: choice over the models you have wired up
shape.answer: the model to call, decided in about a third of a second

use: A slash command or gateway in front of the agent asks Jev which model fits the message, then dispatches. File path lookups go to the cheapest model in the family, work that needs a frontier model goes there, and the bill follows the work rather than the habit. The same shape works in any agent platform: anything that can route a request can read a typed answer first.

title: Inbox pre filtering for AI agents
what: Stop paying a frontier model to read spam.

shape.state: one message, sender and subject kept
shape.question: choice over the buckets you act on
shape.answer: one bucket per message; only the useful ones continue downstream

use: Put the decision in front of the writing. Each message is bucketed as an actionable inquiry, a sponsorship, spam or phishing; spam and phishing are dropped, and only the messages that need a reply reach the model that drafts. In the video's own run, 1,700 messages were sorted for eighteen cents. Keep the state to the fields the question needs, because the rest of the message is a distraction.

code.label: read the headers, drop the noise
code.src:
BUCKETS = {"inquiry": "A real person who needs a reply",
           "sponsor": "A commercial pitch, route to the deals file",
           "spam": "Bulk marketing, no reply",
           "phish": "Attempting to take credentials or money"}

for m in inbox(limit=500):
    state = "From %s. Subject %s. First 400 characters: %s" % (
        m["from"], m["subject"], m["body"][:400])
    ans = decide(state, {"bucket": {"type": "choice", "criteria": BUCKETS,
          "instructions": "Which bucket does this message belong in?"}})["bucket"]
    if ans["choice"] in ("inquiry", "sponsor"):
        hand_to_drafter(m, ans["choice"], ans["confidence"])
